newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty eases on foreign sales after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Zloty eases on foreign sales after rate rise.

text.p: The zloty eased against the basket of currencies in early trade as some foreign players sold Polish paper expecting more rate rises after Tuesday's central bank reverse repo rate rise, dealers said.

The National Bank of Poland (NBP) raised the reverse repo rate by 0.44 point to 22.59 percent saying it wanted to curb reserve money growth and that more rises could be in store if reserve money growth targets had to be defended.
"After yesterday's remarks there is a feeling that the NBP might raise rates further and foreign players are gently shortening positions," said Violetta Gorecka of Pekao SA.

At 0820 GMT the zloty was at 0.74/0.67 percent against the basket of currencies from 0.89/0.77 at opening. It was at 3.3035/55 against the dollar and 1.8775/90 against the mark against 3.2985/15 and 1.8750/70 at opening respectively.
Dealers said it was likely to find first support at around 0.6 percent above parity.

On the money market O/N and T/N offers were flat at 22.60 percent -- pegged to the new NBP reverse repo rate. Dealers expect the central bank to either confirm or raise further the rate at today's 500 million zloty 14-day drainge.

"After the reverse repo rate rise the money market is now firmly pegged to the new level and unless the NBP raises the rate again at today's reverse repo, it will be the new benchmark," said Malgorzata Sikora of ING bank in Warsaw.
The finance ministry is offering 600 million zlotys worth of floating 10-year bonds at a primary tender today.

However, bank and insurance firms dealers said demand for the paper is likely to be small because it was illiquid and rising market interest rates made the investment even less attractive despite their floating interest.
